t: How To Begin Each Day On The Right Classroom Management Foot classroom-management-foot/
q: Can you tell if you’re going to have a long behavior day within the first few minutes of the morning bell? Most teachers can.
The first few minutes of the school day set the behavioral tone for the rest of it. It’s not something you want to cross your fingers over.
Model your opening procedure as if you’re a student. Start outside your classroom–with backpack on–and walk through the entire routine as your students follow closely behind.
Now show your student how not to come in the classroom. Think of the behaviors you’ve seen from your students that you don’t want—and model them.
Watching a classmate successfully complete the procedure cements learning and eliminates excuses for not doing it correctly.

If your class doesn’t typically line up outside your room before school, I recommend you require them to. By having your students come in together, you can more easily associate the inside of your classroom with doing things the right way.
Starting each day with a detailed procedure is a simple way to ensure your students are ready for learning.

t: How To Respond To A Disrespectful Student
q: A disrespectful student can get under a teacher’s skin like almost nothing else.

When a student is disrespectful to you, you have to be willing to lose the battle. In other words, you must resist the urge to admonish, scold, lecture, get even, or otherwise attempt to put the student in their place.
In the immediate moments following the incident, don’t say a word. Simply maintain eye contact with the student and wait.
Your pause and unwillingness to react is unnerving and will leave the student devoid of anything to say. As soon as you break eye contact and walk away, the incident is over.
I recommend bypassing the warning step of your classroom management plan and sending the student directly to time-out.
For overt disrespect, the parents should be notified. A letter home is most effective. It also adds a layer of accountability that lasts beyond the day of the incident.

You didn’t yell, threaten, scold, or lower yourself to the same level of disrespect. You kept your cool and allowed accountability to work, which is the right thing to do for both you and the student.

t: 3 Simple Strategies To Get Your Students To Pay Attention
q: How do you get them to pay attention in a world of instant gratification?
Students love these kinds of things, no doubt about it. But every day? For every lesson? It just isn’t realistic.
Studies show that exercise can boost brain function, improve mood, and increase learning.
Storytelling is a powerful way to introduce lessons. Nothing captures attention as effectively.
Stories also provide deeply layered context for students, linking their memories, emotions, and viewpoints to your lesson objectives.
By holding back the part of the lesson that is most interesting or attractive to students, and dangling it like a carrot, you provide students a compelling reason to pay attention.
Shortcuts, strategies, and solutions abound to make teaching easier, faster, less stressful, more effective, and a lot more fun.

t: Why Straying From Your Classroom Management Plan Is A Gamble You'll Lose Every Time -plan-is-a-gamble/
q: Following your classroom management plan isn’t always easy. But ignoring it is a gamble you’ll lose every time.
Once your students realize that you don’t always follow your classroom management plan, they’ll begin losing respect for you and trust in what you say.
When you’re inconsistent, your students will think you’re playing favorites. “Why did I get a warning for calling out, but she didn’t?” is a common refrain.
If you show a tendency to give in, to let things go, or to lose emotional control, then you’re going to be tested—more every day.
Teachers who forgo their plan find themselves needing to yell, scold, lecture, and the like in order to maintain control.
When you let even small things go, like the occasional calling out, it opens the floodgates to more misbehavior.
Decide to stop rolling the dice and start staying true to your word.
